facts.raw_span: multiple painless nodules on the fingers of both hands
vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts
discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of his right arm and forearm
denied trauma or insect bites
his cow had similar lesions on its teats
3–4 firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema
mild tenderness and increased warmth along the medial right arm and forearm
Dermoscopy (10×) of one nodule showed an erythematous area with central ulceration and crust
yellow-white streaks, brown dots, a structureless whitish area partially surrounding the ulcer, an erythematous ring, and dot vessels

concepts.why: The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker and the presence of similar lesions on his cow's teats, along with the characteristic dermatoscopic findings, suggest Orf virus infection.
The patient's exposure to cows with similar lesions and the development of painless nodules on his hands are consistent with Paravaccinia virus infection.
The patient's contact with cows and the presence of characteristic skin lesions, including vesicles and hemorrhagic crusts, suggest Cowpox virus infection.

rationales.F01: Nodules on the fingers are consistent with zoonotic infections such as Orf virus, Paravaccinia virus, and Cowpox virus.
rationales.F02: Vesicles that rupture and form hemorrhagic crusts are characteristic of Orf virus, Paravaccinia virus, and Cowpox virus infections.
rationales.F05: Similar lesions on the cow's teats suggest a zoonotic infection, with Orf virus being a strong candidate due to its common association with cattle.
rationales.F06: Firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema are typical of Orf virus, Paravaccinia virus, and Cowpox virus infections.
rationales.F08: Dermoscopy findings of an erythematous area with central ulceration and crust are consistent with Orf virus, Paravaccinia virus, and Cowpox virus infections.
rationales.F09: Dermoscopy features such as yellow-white streaks, brown dots, and dot vessels support the diagnosis of a zoonotic infection like Orf virus, Paravaccinia virus, or Cowpox virus.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker and the presence of similar lesions on his cow, along with the specific dermatoscopic findings, support Orf virus infection as the most likely diagnosis.
